output.body:
# HIU, health information user

## In plain words

A health information user is the side of an exchange that wants records it
does not hold. It is identified by a service id, carried in the `X-HIU-ID`
header, which the specification describes as:

> Identifier of the health information user to which the request was intended

The same organisation often holds both roles, one for the records it keeps
and one for the records it wants to read.

## Before you start

You need a consent request the patient has approved, because this role reads
nothing without one.

## What happens

`m3_post_consent_v3_request_init` raises the consent request that this role
begins every exchange with.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say which role a consent request is
raised by and which role it is served against.

## When it goes wrong

Requesting health information on a consent artefact that has expired or been
revoked, which the specification states must not be done.

reply.Text:
**HIU** stands for **Health Information User**. It's a role in ABDM's data exchange model for a system that wants to access health records it doesn't hold itself.

Here's how it works:

- **What it does**: Requests patient consent, then fetches medical records from other healthcare providers (HIP — Health Information Providers)
- **Identified by**: A service ID passed in the `X-HIU-ID` header
- **Requires consent**: An HIU can only read records with explicit patient approval via a consent artefact

**Common scenario**: The same organization often holds both roles — it might be an HIU requesting records from external providers while simultaneously acting as an HIP providing its own records to others.

See the [ABDM glossary](https://abdm-docs.eka.care/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hiu) for more details.
